title: Subdivision Headings

illustrates.quote: j. Treat a row heading preceding a group of subdivisions in the first column as a cell-5 heading. Include this in the transcriber's note with the column headings. Sample: Table changed as follows: (7-5) Subdivision Heading (5-5) Heading of first column (1-1) Heading of second column (3-3) Heading of third column (5-5) Heading of fourth column (7-7) (See ... Sample 11-27: Subdivision Headings on page 11-56.)

print.notes: Print has no column-header row at all: each subdivision title ('Amusement Parks in Florida' / '...in California') spans both columns as its own row, immediately followed by that subdivision's Park/Location data rows -- matching rule 11.18.1 (Subdivision Headings). Run A omitted the print table's rows entirely; run B's transcription of it, re-checked here directly against the PDF page image (p. 338), is correct.
print.printFeatures: Two separate bordered boxes stacked vertically, each with a centered, ruled subdivision-title row spanning the full width of the box; plain data rows beneath.

braille.notes: A transcriber's note (lines 1, 3-5) reads approximately: 'Table changed as follows:' then a heading key involving the words 'State', 'Location' and 'Amusement Park' -- devised headings since none appear in print (rule 11.18.1.k), laid out in the subdivision-heading / first-column-heading / second-column-heading pattern of rule 11.18.1.j (subdivision heading at a 5-5-style margin, column headings at 1-1/3-3-style margins). Each subdivision group ('Amusement Parks in Florida' line 7, 'Amusement Parks in California' line 17) is then blocked as its own cell-5-style heading (indented less than the data rows, at the 'Amusement Park' subdivision level), with its park-name/location pairs following beneath at the stairstep first-column/second-column margins.

uncertain: The exact word-by-word assignment of the 3-line transcriber's-note key (lines 2-4: 'State' / 'Location' / 'Amusement Park') to the rule's column roles is transcribed literally but its precise interpretation is not fully certain.
resolution: print.rows: run A recorded an empty table (a significant miss); run B's 10-row transcription (2 subdivision-title rows + 8 Park/Location data rows) is correct, confirmed directly against the PDF image (p. 338). print.headers set to null (no column-header row exists in print at all -- confirmed against the same image). pdfPages corrected to [338, 339]: both runs missed that the braille half of this sample is on its own separate page (339, printed 11-57), the same print-page/braille-page split used by Samples 11-06, 11-21, and 11-24.
